Fearfulness
fēr'-fūl-nes
n. (dread; the state of being seized with terror)
From fearful and the noun ending -ness. In the Authorized Version the word never means reverence; it is always the dread that overtakes a man against his will, and it is used of a psalmist, a prophet, and the hypocrites in Zion.

Biblical Definition

This is dread, not reverence, and Scripture distributes it carefully. David: “Fearfulness and trembling are come upon me, and horror hath overwhelmed me” (Psa 55:5) — the psalm of the friend's betrayal, where the terror is not of an enemy but of a familiar friend who went with him to the house of God in company. Isaiah, given the vision of Babylon's fall: “My heart panted, fearfulness affrighted me: the night of my pleasure hath he turned into fear unto me” (Isa 21:4). A true prophet is not exhilarated by a vision of judgment; it makes him sick. And then the verse that governs the word: “The sinners in Zion are afraid; fearfulness hath surprised the hypocrites. Who among us shall dwell with the devouring fire? who among us shall dwell with everlasting burnings?” (Isa 33:14). The hypocrites are in Zion — inside the church, in the congregation, at the ordinances — and what surprises them is the discovery that the God they had been near is a consuming fire. Isaiah answers his own question in the next verse: he that walketh righteously and speaketh uprightly shall dwell on high. The same fire that terrifies the hypocrite is the dwelling of the righteous, and the difference is not the fire.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines fearfulness as timorousness; state of being afraid; and fearful as affected by fear, apprehensive, or terrible to behold.

expand to see more

FEARFULNESS, n. Timorousness; timidity.

1. State of being afraid; awe; dread.

FEARFUL, a. Affected by fear; feeling pain in expectation of evil; apprehensive with solicitude.

1. Terrible; impressing fear; frightful; dreadful. It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.

Key Scripture

Isa 33:14 — "The sinners in Zion are afraid; fearfulness hath surprised the hypocrites. Who among us shall dwell with the devouring fire? who among us shall dwell with everlasting burnings?"

Psa 55:5 — "Fearfulness and trembling are come upon me, and horror hath overwhelmed me."

Isa 21:4 — "My heart panted, fearfulness affrighted me: the night of my pleasure hath he turned into fear unto me."

Modern Corruption

Fear of judgment is treated as a manipulation the church should abandon; Isaiah puts it inside Zion and calls it a surprise.

expand to see more

It is now widely held that preaching which produces dread is a failure of the gospel — emotional coercion, unworthy of a God of love. Isaiah 33:14 describes something the modern pulpit rarely produces: fearfulness surprising the hypocrites in Zion, people already inside the congregation discovering that the holiness they had been treating as a comfortable atmosphere is a devouring fire. Our Lord Himself said, fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell. A ministry that has removed this category has not made God safer; it has left the hypocrite undisturbed until the day when the discovery cannot be acted upon.

But Scripture does not leave the believer in dread, and this is where the doctrine must be held whole. The same prophet answers his own question immediately, and the New Testament answers it finally: there is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus, and perfect love casteth out fear. The everlasting burnings are the presence of God, which is torment to the unreconciled and home to the redeemed. Fearfulness is the right response to that presence for a man out of Christ, and it is meant to drive him to Christ, where it becomes reverence and ceases to be terror.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew yir'ah (H3374), fear, dread, reverence; pallatsuth (H6427), shuddering, horror; chaneph (H2611), profane, hypocrite.

expand to see more

Hebrew yir'ah (H3374) — fear, terror, and in other contexts reverence; Psalm 55:5, Isaiah 21:4.

Hebrew pallatsuth (H6427) — shuddering, trembling horror; Isaiah 21:4, Job 21:6, Ezekiel 7:18.

Hebrew ra'ad (H7461) — trembling; Psalm 55:5, fearfulness and trembling.

Hebrew chaneph (H2611) — profane, godless, hypocrite; Isaiah 33:14, whom the fearfulness surprised.

Greek phoberos (G5398) — fearful, terrible; Hebrews 10:31, it is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.

Usage

"“Fearfulness hath surprised the hypocrites” — and they were in Zion."

"“Fearfulness and trembling are come upon me” — a friend had betrayed him."

"“The night of my pleasure hath he turned into fear” — a prophet sickened by his own vision."
